verdict.reasoning: Doctor summarizes: “last three days, you've been having bit of burning pain on passing urine,” which is dysuria for approximately 3 days.
Patient: “it's sort of like a stinging kind of pain… it definitely bothers me when I pee.” Doctor later calls it “burning pain on passing urine.”

Patient: “I also maybe sometimes get some like, pain kind of lower down in my tummy, when I, when I go to the bathroom… sort of cramping.” This supports occasional mild lower abdominal cramp with voiding.
Patient: “there was a little bit of blood earlier today.” This is a small amount of hematuria earlier today.
Patient: “It does kind of… it smells a bit weird I guess.” This indicates malodorous urine.

Frequency: Patient: “I don't think so, I haven't noticed that.” Flank/back pain: Patient denies pain moving to back or flanks (“No, not really, no.”). Nausea/vomiting: Patient: “no, not at all.” Fever: Patient: “No, no, no fever, no.”
Bowels: Patient: “I think so, yeah, it seems [ok]” and specifically denies diarrhoea/loose stool: “no, not that I've noticed at all.”

Sexually active: Patient: “yeah I am.” Regular partner of about 2 months: “I've had a boyfriend for about a, a couple of months now, yeah.” This matches sexually active with a new boyfriend for ~2 months.
Contraception: Patient: “yeah, we use condoms.”
Doctor: “Have you noticed any other discharge from, from down below?” Patient: “I haven't noticed anything.” This supports no vaginal discharge.
Patient: “Uh, couple of weeks ago.” Doctor: “Three weeks ago, OK.” Described in transcript as a couple/three weeks ago, consistent with approximately 2–3 weeks.

Doctor asks about pregnancy: Patient: “Uh, I don't think so, I don't.” Doctor: “Is there any chance you could be pregnant perhaps?”… then advises pregnancy test only if worried. This reflects pregnancy considered unlikely.
STI screen: Patient: “Don't think I've ever, I don't think I've ever had one.”
Patient: “in the past I've had some uh, some IBS.”
Doctor: “Do you take any regular medications?” Patient: “Uh, no…” This supports no regular medications.
Same exchange: “I did… a couple of days ago, try some over the counter bicarbonate… but it wasn't really helping.”
Patient: “yeah, I'm allergic to, Clindamycin.” Doctor: “what happens…?” Patient: “I get some like a… swelling, basically.”
Doctor asks about family history “related to kidneys, bladder, bowels, guts?” Patient: “no I don't think so, not… anything I know about.”
Living situation: “I live in a flat near my college, with a couple of like friends of mine.” Student and subject: “I'm a student… I'm studying biology.”
Smoking/alcohol: Patient: “I don't smoke, I do drink, like on the weekends, yeah.” Doctor: “so socially, OK.”
Doctor: “I think probably [you] do have what we call a simple UTI or urinary tract infection, bladder infection.” This corresponds to acute uncomplicated cystitis based on symptoms.
The transcript notes sexual activity, condom use, no STI screen, and LMP, but the doctor does not state that sexual health counseling is needed or plan it explicitly.
Doctor: “I'll give you a course of antibiotics today. Something, called either Nitrofurantoin, or Trimethoprim. And it's normally a three day course. So, one tablet, twice a day, for three days.”
Doctor: “I also advise you to drink plenty of fluids… You can try, cranberry juice, that can sometimes help with your symptoms.”

Doctor: “if you're still not better, by the end of this week, I want you to give me a call or come back… Things to look out for would be… high temperatures, a back pain… generally feeling more unwell… do give me a call if you're having any concerns.”
Regarding sex: Doctor: “if you can try and avoid it, I think that'd be sensible… I would recommend you to continue using barrier contraception, but if you can avoid it while your symptoms clear up.”
Although STI history is discussed, the doctor does not offer an STI screen or include it in the plan in the transcript.
Doctor: “if… you are worried about the pain… then I'd always advise getting a pregnancy test, to rule out pregnancy.” This matches considering a home urine pregnancy test if there is concern.
